name: multi_factor_composite_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, sharp 30-90 second institutional selling episodes create a simultaneous multi-signal footprint: price drops below the intraday VWAP (VWAP z-score turns deeply negative), the 2-minute RSI enters oversold territory as the speed of descent triggers fast oscillators, and 3-minute momentum confirms the downward impulse. When all three of these independently-computed signals reach extreme readings simultaneously, it indicates algorithmic stop-loss cascades have temporarily overwhelmed NIFTY's resting buy-side order flow — creating a reversion setup as VWAP-benchmarked algorithms and market makers begin accumulating at far-from-fair-value prices. The volume amplifier ensures we only act on confirmed institutional activity, not noise.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: Cumulative VWAP from session open — no lookback needed, resets each day. The reference price all institutional algorithms benchmark against.

indicators.name: vwap_zscore
indicators.purpose: Rolling 120-bar (10-min) z-score of VWAP deviation. Original used 60-bar on 1-min = 60-min window. Compressed to 10 min because we're trading 15-120s holds and want the normalization to reflect current session volatility regime, not the entire day's history. 10 min captures ~2-3 prior swing cycles relevant to our hold time.

indicators.name: rsi_24
indicators.purpose: 24-bar (2-min) RSI. Original used RSI(14) on 1-min bars = 14-min RSI. Compressed to 2 min because we're detecting fast oversold/overbought extremes within our 15-120s hold window. A 2-min RSI captures the exact exhaustion pattern we're trading rather than a multi-hour slow oscillator.

indicators.name: rel_volume
indicators.purpose: Relative volume vs 120-bar (10-min) baseline. Original used SMA(20) on 1-min = 20-min baseline. 10 min on 5s bars is comparable — establishes the typical volume level for the current part of the session. Acts as confidence multiplier: signals during high-volume bars are more reliable.

indicators.name: momentum_36
indicators.purpose: 3-minute (36-bar) raw return. Replaces the original’s index_alignment signal since we ARE trading NIFTY — no need for cross-asset alignment. 3-min momentum captures the directional impulse we are fading: if NIFTY has been falling for 3 min, our oversold buy is more justified. Normalized to [−1,1] by dividing by 0.003 (0.3% = extreme 3-min NIFTY move). The consensus sub-signal threshold of ±0.05 on the normalized value corresponds to ±0.015% raw return — a mild directional filter intentionally set loose to preserve trade frequency in this mean-reversion strategy.

indicators.name: vix_regime_score
indicators.purpose: VIX regime dampener: neutral at VIX=20, positive in calm markets (<20), negative in fear (>20). When VIX > 25, mean reversions become less predictable as fear selling can gap through any support, so we halve the composite when vix_score < -0.5.

indicators.name: composite_score
indicators.purpose: Weighted mean-reversion composite. Positive = oversold (buy CE), negative = overbought (buy PE). VWAP and momentum carry equal weight (0.35 each) because they capture price extremes at different timescales; RSI is slightly lower (0.30) as it lags at 5s resolution.

conditions: at least 2 of 3 directional sub-signals confirm oversold: (vwap_zscore < -0.1) AND/OR (rsi < 50) AND/OR (momentum_norm < -0.05) — where momentum_norm = raw_3min_return / 0.003, so -0.05 normalized corresponds to -0.015% raw 3-minute return (mild directional confirmation, intentionally loose to preserve trade frequency in a mean-reversion strategy)
buy_ce.confirmation: All conditions met simultaneously on a single 5s bar close

conditions: at least 2 of 3 directional sub-signals confirm overbought: (vwap_zscore > 0.1) AND/OR (rsi > 50) AND/OR (momentum_norm > 0.05) — where momentum_norm = raw_3min_return / 0.003, so +0.05 normalized corresponds to +0.015% raw 3-minute return (symmetric with buy_ce threshold)
buy_pe.confirmation: All conditions met simultaneously on a single 5s bar close

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points. If a multi-signal oversold reading is genuinely at a reversion point, NIFTY should not continue adverse by >8 spot pts within 15-120s. If it does, the selldown is structural (e.g., macro event) not a fading opportunity — aligned with typical 2-min adverse move of 5-10 pts (Table 10.4).
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points. A genuine multi-signal oversold reversion on NIFTY typically bounces 15-25 spot pts in the first 1-2 minutes; 7 option pts captures ~60% of the median bounce at 1:1.75 R:R, leaving upside on the table but ensuring a reasonable hit rate.

filters.vix_filter: VIX > 25 halves signal weight (vix_damp = 0.5); still trades but threshold effectively doubles
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:25 IST (skip pre-open noise and EOD liquidity squeeze)
filters.volume_filter: Relative volume amplifier: signal scaled by 1.0 + 0.3 * clip(rel_vol, 0, 1)
filters.spread_filter: N/A — limit order execution at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — multi-factor consensus harder to crowd than single-indicator strategies; mean reversion at extreme readings is a structural market microstructure edge

adaptation_notes: Original was on FnO stocks at 1-min bars holding 15-90 min. Three key changes: (1) Replaced index_alignment signal with 3-min NIFTY momentum since we ARE trading the index — no cross-asset alignment needed. (2) Compressed RSI from 14-min to 2-min, and VWAP z-score window from 60-min to 10-min, because our hold time is 15-120s not 15-90 min. (3) The original had trailing stops and composite-cross exits — replaced with fixed stop/target in premium points because 5s holds cannot track composite score evolution. Volume remains as amplifier not consensus signal since at 5s bars NIFTY volume is noisy.
weaknesses: NIFTY 5s volume is extremely noisy — relative volume signal may fire on cross-exchange arbitrage prints rather than genuine institutional flow
2-min RSI at 5s resolution has 24 samples — at the edge of statistical reliability for mean-reversion signals
Mean reversion trades compete with the same structural edge as many algos; signals may be crowded near VWAP deviation extremes
VIX dampener introduces regime dependence — strategy will be muted during high-volatility sessions when most mean-reversion setups actually occur
